pghv.ponder.brass_cooling_fan.text_1: The Brass Transformer Fan is mounted and powered just like the Andesite one, but controls itself
pghv.ponder.brass_cooling_fan.text_2: Its value field on top sets the target temperature of the transformer instead of a speed
pghv.ponder.brass_cooling_fan.text_3: While the transformer is cold, the fan stands still and saves power
pghv.ponder.brass_cooling_fan.text_4: When the transformer gets warmer than the target, the fan speeds up on its own - at full speed 25 °C above it
pghv.ponder.brass_cooling_fan.text_5: It turns twice as fast and cools twice as strongly as the Andesite fan
pghv.ponder.brass_cooling_fan.text_6: Once the transformer has cooled down, it slows down and stops again
pghv.ponder.brass_cooling_fan_overheat.t: If the transformer still gets too hot, the Brass fan can disconnect it using a Servo and a High Voltage Switch
If the switch moves the wrong way, right-click the socket with a Wrench to reverse the servo direction
The round socket at the bottom right carries servo supply +, servo - and the control signal
Right-click the fan socket with a Data Cable, then plug it into a Data Socket Box
Right-click blocks in between to lay the cable on the floor or a wall; otherwise it hangs
Wire the connectors on top of the box to the Servo: + to coil +, - to coil -, control to control
After each wire, Power Grid starts the next one at the clicked terminal: sneak + right-click into the air before starting the next wire
The Servo turns the shaft of a High Voltage Switch in the transformer's supply line
At 155 °C the protection trips: the Servo turns and opens the switch
Once it has cooled below 100 °C, the Servo turns back and the switch closes again
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_1: The Cooling Fan is mounted on a large side of a Power Grid Medium Transformer
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_2: No matter which cell you click, it snaps onto the whole 2x2 face
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_3: Right-click it with a Wrench to move the panel: front, middle or back
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_4: Power is connected to the two ceramic pins at the bottom left
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_5: At 240 V it runs at full speed and draws its rated 300 W
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_6: The value field on top sets the speed from 0 to 100 %%, just like a Rotation Speed Controller
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_7: The slower it turns, the less power it draws: half speed needs only a quarter
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_8: The air flow cools the transformer behind it, so it can carry more power continuously without overheating
pghv.ponder.cooling_fan.text_9: All four cells blow air forwards and push entities away
pghv.ponder.tag.high_voltage.description: Transformer cooling, overheat protection and multi-core underground cables
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_1: Cable Boxes form the two ends of an underground cable: three terminals on top, a cable socket on the side
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_2: Lay it with Underground Cable. Its three cores determine the terminal colours and the resistance of each conductor
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_3: Right-click the first box to start
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_4: Right-click the ground to set anchor points: for corners...
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_6: Right-click the second box to connect. The boxes turn their sockets towards the cable; one cable item is used per block
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_7: The cable lies on the ground. Inside solid blocks it runs underground and stays invisible
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_8: Each core is a separate conductor: terminal 1 to terminal 1, 2 to 2 and 3 to 3. The terminal caps show the core colour
pghv.ponder.underground_cable.text_9: With Engineer's Goggles a box shows the cores, the resistance of each core, the length and whether it is connected
